subject: SpectraAI — post-call deep qualification: latency/throughput, model fit, next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@spectra.ai>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@spectra.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jan 2029 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SpectraAI post-call: deep qualification recap and proposed next steps

Hi Alyssa / Tom — thanks again for carving time this morning. Quick recap from our side (keeps internal and external aligned):

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Productionizing multi-turn summarization + live ranking for search over large internal docs. Critical: sub-200ms p95 latency on short queries (<=128 tokens) for UI interactions, and burstable throughput for batch scoring (nightly runs ~10M tokens).
- Accuracy trade-offs: SpectraAI wants to keep the 13B base for quality but will consider 4-bit q4/hybrid quant if it preserves top-k recall for summaries.
- Compliance: SOC2 + contract terms around log retention (30 days by default, longer under BAA/HIPAA if needed).

Technical constraints called out during the call
- Average request size: 40 tokens; tail cases up to 1,024 tokens for exports.
- Concurrent active users expected: 250 peak, predicted burst to 1k during daytime events.
- Nightly batch scoring window: 02:00-05:00 PT (can use Dedicated burst capacity).
- On-premises integration: initial deployment on Redwood Hosted, with Dedicated reserved capacity for production in Q3. Private/VPC for regulated data later this year if needed.

Redwood’s proposed fit and immediate asks
- Pilot: Hosted endpoints using a 13B model (we’ll provide a quantized candidate for perf testing) to validate latency SLOs for interactive flows.
- For production throughput and predictable p95: Dedicated pool (multi-A100 equivalent) with autoscale headroom for nightly batch.
- KV-prefix caching recommended for conversational flows to avoid re-tokenizing context; we’ll enable prefix caching on the test endpoints.
- Suggested SLO targets (for pilot conversation): 95th percentile latency <= 120ms for <=128-token requests; 99th percentile <= 300ms. Nightly batch throughput target: support 10–12k tokens/sec aggregated across the pool during the 02:00-05:00 window.

Attachments: I’ve attached the sample latency CSV you shared and our SLO proposal matrix (redwood_slo_matrix_v1.pdf).

Next steps (owners & ETA)
- Redwood action: provide quantized 13B candidate and hosted endpoint + test harness by Tue 2029-01-16 — Priyom (owner).
- SpectraAI action: share representative sample traffic (anonymized) and target recall metrics for summaries by Fri 2029-01-19 — Alyssa (owner).
- Joint: schedule a perf run and topology readout (2 hours) for week of 2029-01-22 — Monica to coordinate.

If that matches your expectations, we’ll kick off the pilot setup. If any detail above is off, correct me and I’ll update the action list.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
If helpful, here’s a short runbook preview: attachment: redwood_slo_matrix_v1.pdf

From: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@spectra.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Keller <tom.keller@spectra.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jan 2029 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SpectraAI post-call: deep qualification recap and proposed next steps

Thanks Priyom — good writeup and aligns with our notes. A few clarifications and priorities from SpectraAI: 

Clarifications
- The UI p95 requirement is firm at <=120ms for 95% of interactive requests; we can accept longer tails for the 99th percentile.
- Nightly batch is flexible on start time but must complete within a 3-hour window. The 10–12k tokens/sec target is a good starting point.
- We will share an anonymized sample of traffic and the scoring labels. Expect that by EOD Fri (internal legal sign-off pending).

Priorities for the pilot (in order)
1) Latency validation on Hosted with the quantized 13B (quality must be within 1–2% of baseline recall).
2) Throughput validation in a Dedicated-like topology (we’re okay with a simulated Dedicated run during the pilot).
3) Compliance checklist and data retention options — Procurement will loop in a legal contact if we move past pilot.

One logistics ask: can Redwood provide a simple run command or script for the perf harness so our infra team can run it in our staging environment? Also please include the exact model repo / quantization hash you’ll be testing.

Thanks — will confirm traffic sample timeline shortly.

—
Alyssa Cheng
Head of Platform Engineering, SpectraAI
Alyssa: attaching the traffic sample in a follow-up (spectra_latency_sample.csv) when legal clears it.

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@spectra.ai>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@spectra.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jan 2029 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SpectraAI post-call: deep qualification recap and proposed next steps

Internal engineering notes for the perf run (FYI / Priyom to include in test artifact):

Topology options to test (we should include 3):
A) Hosted low-latency path: single-shard 13B q4 variant on NVLink-connected GPUs with continuous batching disabled for interactive routes; set max_batch_ms = 5 to prioritize latency. Expected: p95 ~ 90–140ms depending on sequence len and tokenizer overhead.
B) Dedicated production pool: multi-shard stripe across 4x A100-40GB equiv with autoscale headroom. Enable KV cache and prefix caching for conversations; use dynamic batching during off-peak to maximize throughput. Expected: steady-state aggregate throughput 8–15k tokens/sec for scoring when batching is enabled.
C) Hybrid fallback path: smaller 7B quant variant for degraded-mode when Dedicated capacity constrained; provide model routing policy with automated fallback on 5-minute outage. This keeps UI available albeit with slightly lower summary fidelity.

Perf harness deliverables we should hand over:
- run_harness.sh: (curl-based, multi-threaded client simulating 250 concurrent short queries + 5 batch workers for nightly window) — include parameters for token distribution, concurrency, and warm-up.
- model_hash.txt with exact repo:quant_hash we’re testing and tokenizer spec.
- SLO measurement script that emits p50/p95/p99 plus token throughput and GPU utilization traces.

Security/compliance notes
- For data-in-transit and at-rest: we’ll document KMS + VPC egress controls for Private deployments. For pilot on Hosted, add a retention toggle to avoid persisting raw prompts; logs retained for 30 days by default.

I’ll draft the run_harness and model_hash files and attach to the pilot ticket. Priyom — can you include estimated GPU count for the Dedicated sim (4x A100 equiv as baseline) and a cost ballpark for a 3-month pilot?

Monica

From: Tom Keller <tom.keller@spectra.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Alyssa Cheng <alyssa@spectra.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, procurement@spectra.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2029 14:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SpectraAI post-call: deep qualification recap and proposed next steps

All — thanks. Two procurement/legal asks before we proceed to pilot: 1) a standard MSA + Data Processing Addendum (we’d like to see Redwood’s SOC2 report), and 2) a note on data retention options (we prefer 90 days for logs if possible under Enterprise plan). If Redwood can send a draft MSA or a marketplace listing with contract terms, procurement will prioritize review.

Alyssa: We’ll aim to get the traffic sample over by EOD Fri; if legal drags, we’ll at least provide tokenized anonymized rows.

Priyom / Monica: once we have the sample, can you provide a calibrated perf schedule (time + expected run length) so our infra team can block a 3-hour window? Also please include the run_harness.sh mentioned.

Tom
Director of Ops, SpectraAI
